hazards.control: Bleed the tubing and casing to zero and verify before breaking any connection.

name: Rod pump (insert pump, cut-away)
function: The positive-displacement pump at the tubing tail, stroked by the rod string: a plunger in a barrel with a traveling valve in the plunger and a standing valve in the barrel.

tabs.overview: The insert pump is run on the rods and seats in a seating nipple in the tubing on a hold-down. Upstroke: the traveling valve closes and the plunger lifts the fluid above it while the standing valve opens and the barrel fills from below. Downstroke: the standing valve closes and the traveling valve opens as the plunger passes down through the fluid. A gas anchor below the intake separates free gas so the pump fills with liquid. The cut-away shows the barrel, plunger mid-stroke, both ball-and-seat valves in their cages, the valve rod and coupling, the hold-down and seating nipple, and the gas anchor, with the tubing as ghost context.
tabs.engineering: API 11AX designations name bore, barrel and plunger type, and seating. Displacement is bore area times stroke times strokes per minute less slippage; deep wells use smaller bores to limit rod load.
tabs.connections: Rod string above; seating nipple in the tubing (UC); gas anchor below.
tabs.safety: Pulled with the rods on a rig; the well is killed or the tubing isolated first.
tabs.evidence: PetroWiki sucker-rod lift, ESP, and gas lift pages (S39, S40, S41); API 11AX, 11E, 11S, 11V (S43 to S46); field practice (S9). Generic geometry; not an OEM design.
tabs.operations: Spaced so the plunger does not tag the standing valve; monitored by dynamometer.
tabs.failure_modes: Valve leaks (worn balls and seats), plunger and barrel wear from sand, gas lock, stuck plunger.

standards.paraphrase: Subsurface pump assemblies, components, and fittings.
